the incorporation of Sr2 + and Ni3 + in perov-skite-type LaFeO3 − d increases oxygen deficiency, ionic transport and thermal expansion at elevated temperatures, and leads to a lower stability as reflected by the narrowing of the solid-solution region at 1373 K in air.

the incorporation of Sr2 + and Ni2 + in LaFeO3 − δ perovskite increases the oxygen deficiency and oxygen transport at elevated temperatures and lowers the thermodynamic stability of La1 - ySryFexNixO3- δ (y < 0.2, x = 0–0.4) ceramics.
In summary, our research is concerned with

a systematic study of structural, thermal, electrical, and transport properties of La1 - ySry(Fe1 - xNix)O3 - δ perovskites with a view to their application as oxygen permeable membranes in air separation.

the effect of strontium and/or nickel doping on the structural, thermal expansion, transport and defect properties of perovskite LaFeO3 − doped with strontium, nickel and both additives, which are of interest for oxygen separation membranes and catalysis.
the development of a new family of perovskite materials with a high mixed ionic and electronic conductivity, high thermal expansion, low Seebeck coefficient and a high oxygen permeation rate.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
strontium and, especially, nickel doping of LaFeO3 − d are beneficial for the mixed conductivity, oxygen transport and thermal stability of perovskite ceramics.

the incorporation of nickel in (La,Sr)FeO3 − doping leads to an increase in ionic conductivity and a decrease in thermodynamic stability of the solid solution, while the Seebeck coefficients and oxygen transport are not strongly affected.
the nickel doping of the La1−ySryFeO3 − d perovskites leads to a mixed-conduction material with high ionic conductivity and low thermal expansion coefficient.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the substitution of nickel for iron in perovskites La1 − SrySryFe1−xNixO 3−δ (x ≈ 1) is not beneficial for the oxygen transport at elevated temperatures but it is promising for the application at intermediate temperatures.

nickel doping of La1 + xSrxFe1 − zNizO3 − z − δ perovskites is a good way of improving the mixed ionic-electronic conductivity at elevated temperatures, while maintaining the high thermodynamic stability of the material.

the incorporation of nickel in LaFeO3 − δ perovskite is not detrimental to the mixed ionic-electronic conductivity and oxygen permeation flux, but it can be useful for the improvement of the thermal expansion properties and the stability in air.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the (La,Sr)Fe1 − NixO3 δ solid solutions are attractive candidates for oxygen separation membranes and thermoelectric generators, but require optimization of the chemical composition, microstructure and operating conditions.

the incorporation of Ni into La1 −ySryFeO3 −δ perovskites leads to a decrease in the thermodynamic stability, oxygen deficiency and ictonic conductivity, and a rise in the thermal expansion coefficients, while having no negative effect on the average oxidation state at low temperatures.
(La,Sr) (Fe,Ni) O3 −  δ perovskite ceramics with high ionic conductivity and moderate thermal expansion are promising candidates for membrane reactors in chemical and energy technologies.
